1. (Currently Amended) A proofed frozen dough comprising: (a) a dough mixture of flour, water, and optionally additives, the dough mixture defining a dough matrix; (b) gas bubbles dispersed throughout the dough matrix, wherein the gas bubbles are produced during proofing and comprise carbon dioxide; (c) a spent yeast component that has been metabolically active during proofing and is substantially depleted of fermentative capacity; and (d) a preserved yeast component that remains metabolically viable and capable of fermentation after freezing and thawing.

2. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough comprises about 1 to about 8 wt.% of the spent yeast component.

3. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the spent yeast component comprises yeast from cream yeast, compressed yeast, semi-dry yeast, frozen yeast, active dry yeast, instant yeast, or a combination thereof.

4. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 3, wherein the yeast has been spent during proofing.

5. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the spent yeast component has a yeast vitality of less than 25 wt.% of its initial vitality.

6. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the preserved yeast component has a yeast vitality of at least 50 wt.% of its initial vitality.

7. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough comprises about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the preserved yeast component.

8. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the preserved yeast component comprises encapsulated yeast, fat-coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof, and wherein the preserved yeast component is physically separated from the spent yeast component.

9. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough has a volume, and wherein the gas bubbles make up about 30 to about 90 wt.% of the volume of the frozen dough.

10. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough has a density of about 0.2 to about 0.5 g/cm³.

11. (Currently Amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the gas bubbles comprise gas produced by the spent yeast component during proofing, and wherein the preserved yeast component does not substantially contribute to gas production during the proofing stage.

12. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the frozen dough is in its final shape and form for baking.

13. (Currently Amended) A method for making a frozen dough product, the method comprising: (a) mixing dough ingredients to produce a dough composition, the dough ingredients comprising: i. water; ii. flour; iii. a first yeast that is unencapsulated and metabolically active; and iv. a second yeast that is encapsulated or protected; (b) proofing the dough under conditions wherein the first yeast is metabolically spent and produces carbon dioxide, and wherein the second yeast remains substantially preserved and metabolically viable; and (c) freezing the dough after proofing.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein at least 60 wt.% of the first yeast is spent during proofing.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein at least 50 wt.% of the second yeast is preserved during proofing.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 1 to about 7 wt.% of the first yeast.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the second yeast.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the second yeast is different from the first yeast and is physically separated from the first yeast during mixing.

19. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein the second yeast comprises encapsulated yeast, fat coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the mixing comprises mixing the water, flour, and first yeast for a first period of time, adding the second yeast and mixing the dough ingredients for a second period of time, wherein the first period of time is longer than the second period of time, and wherein the second yeast is added after the first yeast has begun fermentation.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 20, wherein the second period of time is from about 1 to about 2 minutes.

22. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising: shaping and cutting the dough to produce a pizza crust prior to proofing; freezing the pizza crust; and applying toppings to the frozen pizza crust.

23. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising refrigerating the dough after freezing.

24. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the dough is refrigerated for from about 12 hours to about 7 days.

25. (Currently Amended) A method for making a leavened bakery product, the method comprising: (a) mixing dough ingredients to produce a dough, the dough ingredients comprising: i. water; ii. flour; iii. a first yeast that is unencapsulated and metabolically active; and iv. a second yeast that is encapsulated or protected; (b) proofing the dough to produce a proofed dough, wherein the first yeast is spent during the proofing and produces carbon dioxide, and wherein the second yeast is preserved during the proofing and remains metabolically viable; (c) freezing the proofed dough; and (d) baking the dough to produce the leavened bakery product, wherein the second yeast contributes to leavening during the baking step.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the second yeast is different from the first yeast and is physically separated from the first yeast during mixing.

27. (Original) The method of claim 25, wherein the second yeast comprises encapsulated yeast, fat coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof.

28. (Original) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough does not comprise chemical leaveners.

29. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough has a first volume before the proofing step, a second volume after the proofing step, and a third volume after the baking step, and wherein the third volume is at least 50 wt.% greater than the second volume.

30. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 29, wherein the third volume is greater than the second volume due at least in part to an activity of the second yeast during the baking step, and wherein the second yeast provides supplemental leavening beyond that provided by carbon dioxide produced during the proofing step.

31. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 20 to about 40 wt.% water and about 50 to about 70 wt.% flour.

32. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 1 to about 7 wt.% of the first yeast.

33. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the second yeast.
